title: Astronauts on the Space Station See 16 Sunrises a Day

scenes.text: Astronauts on the space station see 16 sunrises every single day.
It circles Earth every 90 minutes, at five miles a second. So every 45 minutes, the sun comes up or goes down.
Astronaut Scott Kelly saw nearly eleven thousand sunrises and sunsets in one year. You see about 700.
The station isn't flying. It's falling, so fast and so sideways that it keeps missing the ground.
So the crew sleeps by the clock, not the sun. Because the sun rises sixteen times a day.

description:
Astronauts on the International Space Station see 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every day.
The station orbits Earth about once every 90 minutes at five miles per second, so NASA astronaut Scott Kelly saw 10,944 sunrises and sunsets during his year in space, while people on the ground saw 684.
Would you ever get used to a sunrise every 90 minutes?
first_comment: Would you rather see 16 sunrises a day on the station, or one six-month-long day at the South Pole?
